script:
AddText "The link opens onto an argument already in progress. Somebody reads your transponder code aloud, somebody else asks - twice, and not calmly - what exactly you thought you were fishing for, and your comms officer sits through all of it with the expression of a person who would rather be doing anything else."
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"Be advised, the incident has been logged.\" $PersonRank $personName holds up a slate as though you could read it. \"Hull breach, non-standard munition, recovered intact. It is going to Naval Intelligence, because everything unidentified goes to Naval Intelligence. You will be hearing about the barb.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"Damage assessment is complete and your involvement is not in dispute.\" $PersonRank $personName reads without inflection. \"You will receive a schedule of costs. It will be itemised. One of the items will be the harpoon, which we have kept.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "$PersonRank $personName looks at the puncture, then at you, with the particular patience of someone cataloguing a sin. \"A machine for taking things out of the dark,\" $heOrShe says. \"And you pointed it at people.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"Do not say anything.\" Whoever answers is not angry the way people usually are on this channel. \"We have seen that gear before. We know where it goes and we know what it brings back, and you have just put it through the side of a ship with people in it.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"That,\" says $personName, with something close to admiration, \"is not a weapon. That is a fishing rig.\" A pause. \"Which you fired. At us. What is wrong with you?\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"You have discharged an unregistered device at a vessel of the Diktat.\" $PersonRank $personName does not blink. \"I am required to ask whether this was deliberate. I am not required to believe the answer.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"There is a form for this.\" $PersonRank $personName sounds almost pleased about it. \"There is not a form for this, actually. I have checked. I am going to have to write to someone about the fact that there is no form for this.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"You put a hook in us,\" says $personName, in the flat voice of somebody who has had a long month and is not going to have a shorter one. \"Not a shot. A hook. We are going to be explaining that to the yard for a year.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

ShowDefaultVisual
AddText "The link is answered by somebody who already has your file open and a more pressing reason to dislike you already on it. The harpoon comes up once, near the end, in a list of things that will be dealt with later."
EndConversation NO_CONTINUE
notes: Fallback for a crew you holed who is hostile over something else entirely - the other rows all want the harpoon itself to be the reason. Lowest score here so every one of them outranks it. It exists because the comm link is highlighted on having been harpooned at all, and a highlighted link with nothing behind it is a dead option.

notes: The patrol sent about a harpooning, arriving. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger, which puts the fleet's own memory in the local scope. Marked as had here rather than at each ending, as the cargo scan does: the patrol is still pursuing while the dialog is open, so a conversation that only counted once it was finished would be reopened the instant the player closed it.

text:
"We have a report of a $faction hull holed by - " $PersonRank $personName stops, checks the screen again, and continues in the voice of somebody who has decided not to editorialise. " - by a fishing implement."

"Damage to fleet property, discharge of a projectile weapon inside a patrolled lane, and whatever the tribunal decides to call the rest of it. Settle it here for $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits and it goes in the file as an accident."

Your ops chief, who has the figure up on a slate before you have asked for it, holds it where only you can see it.

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to."

$PersonRank $personName works through it without looking up. "Discharge of an unregistered device, damage to a registered hull, and an entry under 'munition, description of' that I have had to write out by hand. The schedule for all three comes to $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

$HeOrShe finally looks up, and looks at your ship rather than at you. "Pay it and the file says accident. Don't, and it says something else, and then it stops being mine."

"Tri-Tachyon corporate security. This is a billing matter, and I would ask you to treat it as one."

$PersonRank $personName has the figure ready before your comms officer has finished opening the channel. "Hull damage, survey time, and the recovery of a foreign object from a company vessel. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, settled now, at the pre-litigation rate."

"The post-litigation rate is not a number I am authorised to say out loud."

"Peace be with you. Cut your engines."

$PersonRank $personName looks tired rather than angry, and looks at your rig for rather longer than at your face. "A crew of ours has a hole in their ship, put there by a machine built for reaching into somewhere nothing has any business reaching into."

"The Church will not be pricing that part of it. The repair comes to $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, and that we will take."

"Pay it, and think about the rest on your own time."

"Cut your drive."

$PersonRank $personName is looking at your ship rather than at you, and at one particular part of it. "We know what that is. We know what it reaches into and we know what comes back through when it does."

"There is a hull with a hole in it and a tribute owed for the hole. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Pay that."

"The other thing - the rig, and the water you point it at - is not something anybody takes money about."

"Hold position, friend."

$PersonName is grinning at you through a channel your comms officer has already flagged as unencrypted. "Word is you put a hook in a hull. Not shot it - hooked it. Half of us want to buy you a drink and the other half want the rig off your ship."

"Neither's happening. What is happening is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, and then nobody has to find out how the rest of it goes."

"Heave to for the Sindrian Diktat."

$PersonRank $personName reads the charge as though it were a sentence already handed down. "Discharge of an unregistered device within Diktat space, against a Diktat hull. The administrative penalty is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"The administrative penalty is the favourable outcome. I would take it."

"Persean League patrol. Cut your drive."

$PersonRank $personName has clearly been reading up on the way out to you. "There is no statute for this. There is a statute for discharging a weapon at a member-state hull, and a separate one for damage caused by recovery equipment, and I have decided to apply both."

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Argue it with a committee if you like, but not with me, and not from where your ship is currently sitting."

"Independent patrol. Ease off."

$PersonName sounds like somebody who took this contract for the fuel allowance and is still working out whether it was worth it. "Somebody you hooked filed with us, and filing means I have to fly all the way out here and say a number at you. The number is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Say yes and we can both go back to what we were doing."

text: "You were told the penalty was the favourable outcome." $PersonRank $personName sounds almost sorry. "It was."

$PersonRank $personName checks a reference before answering you properly. "Paid and filed. You are the fishing one."

It is not clear whether that is better or worse than the alternative, and your comms officer very carefully does not offer an opinion.
notes: Paid, and still on speaking terms - so this adds a line and hands the screen to the ordinary conversation menu rather than closing it. Keyed on a second flag from the paying rule rather than the one the script reads, because that one is consumed the moment it is read and this line has to keep working afterwards.

text: The link is accepted somewhere on the other ship and left open, unattended, on what sounds like a compartment being cleared for action. Nobody comes to it.
notes: Refused, and still angry about it. Gated on their hostility rather than on the conversation having happened, so this cannot go on refusing to talk to the player for a month after everyone involved has calmed down.

The affordability check greys the option out and explains why, which is vanilla's own handling and better than hiding it - a player who cannot pay should still see what they could not pay. Safe in the script column because options from every matching rule are added before any of their scripts run.

text: The count comes up short, and the matter is left there.
notes: The catch-all, scored above every job's own line. Reachable only if the hold empties between the option being drawn and the option being taken.

text: You are still owed for $catchreleaseAsk.
notes: No conditions and no score, so every job's own reminder outscores it. It speaks only for a job that has not written one. A bare score: line would be a condition with no tokens left after the score is stripped, which throws on load.

text: One of the drinkers has a slate out and a list on it, and keeps looking at the door as though expecting somebody who knows what they are doing with a net.

"Standing order," $heOrShe says, and turns the slate round. "$catchreleaseAskCap. I am not fussy about who brings them, only that they arrive."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap, on delivery."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the order.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Not my sort of water."

text: $HeOrShe writes something next to the list without looking up. "It will keep."
The slate goes back to the bar top.
$HeOrShe taps the slate. "$catchreleaseAskCap. The order has not changed."

$HeOrShe checks the crates without hurrying, and pays without arguing about it.

$catchreleaseRewardCap, counted out on the bar top.
A cook in a stained whites jacket is arguing with a supplier over a comm slate, losing, and not enjoying it.

options: catchrelease_chef_ask:Ask the cook what the problem is.

text:
"Three things," the cook says, before you have said anything at all. "On one plate. It is $catchreleaseDish and it does not work with two."

"I need $catchreleaseAsk. Not similar. Different. That is the entire idea."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap when they are in my kitchen and not before."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the order.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Find another supplier."

text: "Good. Do not freeze them."
The cook goes back to the comm slate, and back to losing.
"Three," the cook says, without looking up. "$catchreleaseAskCap. It is still three."

The cook unpacks all of it on the bar top, in front of everyone, and spends a long time not saying anything.

"Yes. That is the plate." You are paid $catchreleaseReward, and told to come back in a month, when there will be a different plate.
A young man with a very good jacket and a very cheap drink is explaining something to two people who are not listening, and to a third who left.

options: catchrelease_startup_ask:Let the young man finish his sentence.

text:
"You fish," he says. It is not a question and he does not wait. "Everyone in this sector eats reconstituted protein because nobody has solved logistics. I have solved logistics. What I do not have is a demonstrated inbound."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. That is all. I need to be able to say, truthfully, that it arrived."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap for the first run. There will be more runs."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to the first run.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"No."

text: "Excellent. I will need an invoice. Do you do invoices?"
"That is fine. That is fine. I have other conversations." He does not.
"Still waiting on the inbound," he says, with the brightness of a man who has told somebody a date. "$catchreleaseAskCap."
He counts it twice, photographs it, and pays you $catchreleaseReward without haggling, which from him is alarming.

He is already scrolling. "Right. Right. Now the same again, at volume, because the figure I showed them was not the figure you just delivered."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Same terms, better terms, whatever you want - I have investors now."
"That is a supply chain," he says, to himself more than to you. "That is a supply chain and I have one."
A man in a plain, expensive coat is not drinking, and has been not drinking for some time. He watches the door the way somebody does when they are being paid to be somewhere.

options: catchrelease_butler_ask:Ask the man in the coat who he is waiting for.

text:
"I am buying for a household," he says. "I will not be naming it."

"The requirement is $catchreleaseAsk. I am told that is a difficult number. I am not empowered to lower it."

His expression does not change. "It is to be looked at, you understand. Not eaten. Whether it is a good specimen of its kind is not a question that has been put to me."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap, on presentation."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Accept the commission.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Leave him to it.

text: "Very good." He writes nothing down, which suggests he does not need to.
"Understood." He resumes not drinking.
"The requirement has not changed," he says. "$catchreleaseAskCap."

He does not look at it for long. He looks at the scale.

"That will do." $catchreleaseRewardCap, handed over in a way that suggests he has done this for things far stranger than a fish.
A woman with salt-cracked hands and an academic's posture is sketching something on a slate and covering it whenever anyone walks past.

"I keep a tank," she says. "Larger than is sensible. I am told it is a conservation programme, which is what people call a collection when it has a grant attached."

"What I want is $catchreleaseAsk."

She taps the slate. "Either will do. A perfect one teaches you what the species is meant to be. A ruined one teaches you what is happening to it. I have space for both and no preference between them."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap. And I will not ask where."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to stock the tank.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Not my sort of water."

text: "Keep it wet," she says. "Whichever one you find."
She covers the slate again.
"Still $catchreleaseAsk," she says. "Either sort. I have not become fussier."

She has the tank lid off before the crate is properly open, and does not thank you until everything is in the water.

Then she does, at some length, and pays you $catchreleaseReward.
Two children who should not be in here are conducting negotiations at a corner table. One of them is doing all the talking. The other one has a bucket.

options: catchrelease_duel_ask:Find out what the children want.

text:
"We need two," the loud one says. "For the battle."

The quiet one turns the bucket so you can see into it. There is nothing in the bucket. This does not appear to have discouraged anyone.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. One each. Then they fight."

You point out that they will not fight. This is dismissed as an adult opinion. The payment, when it is produced, is $catchreleaseReward - and it is produced from four pockets, so you understand that it is all of it.
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to supply the battle.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Explain, gently, that fish do not fight.

text: The loud one shakes your hand. The quiet one does not, but does nod, which you gather is the binding part.
They take this well, which is somehow worse.
"Have you got them yet." It is the fourth time today for somebody.

You hand the better of the two to $catchreleaseKid. There is a silence of the kind that precedes either delight or a formal complaint.

$catchreleaseOtherCap declares this unfair. The declaration is noted and ignored.

Between them they produce $catchreleaseReward, which they clearly consider a fortune, and which they are not wrong about.

You hand the better of the two to $catchreleaseKid. There is a silence of the kind that precedes either delight or a formal complaint, and your ops chief takes a step back from the table to be out of the way of either.

It is a serious fish. Both of them go very quiet looking at it, and then $catchreleaseOther empties a pocket onto the table without being asked to.

Between them they produce $catchreleaseReward, which they clearly consider to be a fortune, and about which they are not entirely wrong.

options:
catchrelease_duelLoud:Give the better one to the loud one.
catchrelease_duelQuiet:Give the better one to the quiet one.
notes: Which child gets which fish. The choice cannot be got wrong - the extra is paid for the specimen, not for the guess.

options: catchrelease_duelWait:Tell them you are still looking.

text: Two men are sitting with a tank between them that is far too good for this bar. Neither of them is drinking. Both of them are watching everyone who is.

"You bring the stock," says the one who introduces himself as $catchreleaseLeft. "We supply the rest." He does not say what the rest is. The other one, $catchreleaseRight, taps the ampoule case on the table, which is an answer of sorts.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Two, because it is not much of an event with one."

"Flat fee is $catchreleaseReward. Or you put the fee on one of ours and take double if it walks out. Your call, at the door, not before."

"Bring a good one," the second one adds. "They last longer. That is your business, not ours, but it is your money."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to supply the ring.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Decide you were never here.

text: Neither of them writes anything down. You get the impression that they will remember.
They go back to watching the room. You are no longer part of what they are watching, which is a relief.
"Still two," one of them says, without turning round.

You take the fee. One of them looks briefly disappointed in you, which from a man in this line of work is close to a compliment.

$catchreleaseRewardCap, counted out on the tank lid.

The tank goes in. Something is added to the water from an unlabelled ampoule. Nobody explains what, and the room leans in.

$catchreleaseWager's fish is still moving. Yours was on it. You are paid $catchreleaseReward, and paid promptly, which is the part that tells you they are serious people.

The tank goes in. Something is added to the water from an unlabelled ampoule, nobody explains what it was, and the whole room leans in at once.

It is over quickly, and it is not your side that it is over for. $catchreleaseFoe shrugs at you from across the table. "You picked. That is the whole of it."

You walk your crew out with nothing, which is exactly what you agreed to on the way in.

options:
catchrelease_ringFlat:Hand them over and take the fee.
catchrelease_ringLeft:Put the fee on $catchreleaseLeft's fish.
catchrelease_ringRight:Put the fee on $catchreleaseRight's fish.
notes: The one wager in the mod. Backing a side pays double or nothing, and the odds are read off the specimen handed over rather than off a coin.

text: A woman at the end of the bar is dressed for somewhere else entirely and is not troubled by this. She has been looking at you for a while, and it is not the look you would assume.

"I have a client," she says. "That is the word I am going to use and we are both going to leave it there."

"He wants a fish. A real one, out of the water, not off a menu. $catchreleaseAskCap - that is the floor, and I want you to understand that it is a floor."

You ask what it is for. She looks at you with enormous patience.

"$catchreleaseRewardCap," she says. "More if it is bigger. That is the entire arrangement and it is a very good one."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the arrangement.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"I don't think so."

text: "Discreetly," she says. "Not secretly. There is a difference and the difference is paperwork."
"Of course." She is already looking past you at the door.
"Still $catchreleaseAsk," she says. "He has not become less specific."

She does not open the container in the bar. She weighs it, in her hands, the way somebody does when they have done it before.

$catchreleaseRewardCap changes hands, and she is gone before you have counted it.

She does not open the container in the bar. She weighs it, in her hands, the way somebody does when they have done it before.

"Oh, that is over," she says. "That is comfortably over."

$catchreleaseRewardCap changes hands, and she is gone before you have counted it.
A researcher with an Academy lanyard she has stopped bothering to hide is working through a stack of sample logs and marking almost all of them as useless.

"Everyone brings me good ones," she says. "Whole ones. Beautiful ones. They are worthless to me and I have stopped being polite about it."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Barely holding together. If it looks like it is about to stop being a fish, that is the specimen."

She notices your expression. "A stable one tells me what a fish is. I know what a fish is. I want to know what is happening to them, and the ones it is happening to are the ones that come up wrong."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap. The Academy will not ask where either."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to bring her a bad one.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Leave her to it.

text: "Do not stabilise it in transit," she says. "Please. It has happened."
She goes back to marking things useless.
"$catchreleaseAskCap," she says. "Worse is better. I am aware of how that sounds."

She holds it up to the light, and whatever she sees through it makes her sit down.

"Thank you. Genuinely." $catchreleaseRewardCap, and a promise you will be in a footnote.
Somebody has set up two lamps and a very expensive lens pointed at an empty chair, and is explaining to the bar staff that it will only take a minute.

options: catchrelease_tuber_ask:Ask what the lamps are for.

text:
"Do not look at the lens," he says, meaning that you should. "I do fishing content. It is a growing vertical."

"I need $catchreleaseAsk. To hold up. That is the shot - I hold it up, I say the name, people find out fish are real."

"I cannot pay what a buyer pays. What I can do is $catchreleaseReward, all of which was sent to me by people who want to be in a video."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to be in the video.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Step out of the shot.

text: "Amazing. Amazing. Can you say that again with the lamps on?"
"No, that is fair. That is completely fair." He is still filming.
"No rush," he says, in the voice of a man with a posting schedule. "$catchreleaseAskCap."
He films it from four angles and pays you $catchreleaseReward out of a box of things people have sent him.

He films the specimen for a long time, and then goes quiet in the way you recognise from people looking at a number that has not moved since yesterday.

"It did fine," he says eventually. "Fine is the worst thing that can happen to you. Nobody stops scrolling for a healthy fish." He looks up at you, and at your hold behind you, with an idea already fully formed.

"Can you get me a bad one? On purpose? $catchreleaseAskCap - something that looks like it is arguing with being alive. $catchreleaseRewardCap, and I will credit your ship by name, which I appreciate is not the same as paying you more."

"That," he says, watching the playback, "is the thumbnail. That is the whole video and I have not shot the video."

$catchreleaseRewardCap, out of a box of things people have sent him.
Three people in matching, unremarkable coats are sharing one drink between them and have not touched it. They are waiting, and they are not impatient.

options: catchrelease_cult_ask:Ask the three in the coats what they are waiting for.

text:
One of them says a name. Not yours - the fish's.

"$catchreleaseSpecies," they repeat, when you do not answer immediately. "One. Whole."

You ask what for. There is a pause of exactly the length of somebody deciding not to be offended, and then the same sentence again, with the same emphasis, as though the problem had been the volume.

"$catchreleaseRewardCap," the second one adds, and produces it, and puts it on the table, and leaves it there while you think about it.
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to find it.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Decline, politely.

text: None of them thanks you. All three of them nod at the same time, which is worse.
They do not seem to mind. You get the strong impression they will be here when you come back.
"$catchreleaseSpecies," one of them says. That is the whole of the conversation.

They do not open it. One of them puts a hand flat on the lid and leaves it there for rather too long.

$catchreleaseRewardCap, pushed across the table. Nobody says what it is for, and by now you have stopped expecting them to.

notes: They open the link themselves the first time and never again - being asked once is a distress call and being asked on every pass is a toll. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger.

text: "$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestPitch"
notes: The pitch is read off the fleet's own memory so one row serves every kind of trouble it could be in.

text: They send over what little they know about the local water and settle in to wait. Whatever else happens out here they will be exactly where you left them.
They take it the way anyone takes it. The link closes without anything further being said, and the light over them goes out.
notes: Declining ends the offer. Nothing was spawned to carry it, so there is nothing to tidy away - the mark comes off and the fleet carries on with whatever it was already doing.

text: They are exactly where you left them and they have not stopped watching the water.

notes: The option exists only when the hold can pay for it - updateData counts it and the flag it sets is what this row is really asking about.

text: The crates go across without ceremony. Somebody aboard says something that does not come through cleanly and several other people laugh at it.
The link closes. They go back to waiting.

Paying or refusing sets the long one through the command.

text:
"You are the one with the rope." It is not a question, and $PersonRank $personName does not sound angry so much as tired of the whole shift.

"We are not the navy and we are not going to stand here pretending that we are. There is a hole in a hull that was surveyed clean this morning, and somebody has to pay a yard to close it again. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonDamagesDGS credits, and we log the whole thing as debris and your name never appears on it."

Behind $himOrHer, somebody is still working on the hole.

notes: Third hole. They have stopped talking to you and started talking about you - the call to whatever patrol is in the system goes out with the harpooning itself, so this is only what it looks like from your end.

text:
Your sensors officer picks the hull out of the clutter well before you are close enough to see it, and does not sound pleased about the reading. "Cruiser, $catchreleaseWreckHull, cold all the way through. No transponder. The registry plate has been ground off, which people do not generally do by accident."

There is a hole in the dorsal plating with half a kilometre of line still through it. Your ops chief puts a light on it as you come alongside. The head went in from outside. The plating around it is bent the other way.

text:
The boarding party report back in the flat voice people use when they would rather not be saying any of it. The berths are made up. The galley is stocked. There is a half-finished meal on the mess table that has not rotted, because nothing in here has.

"Nobody aboard, $playerSirOrMadam," your ops chief says. "Nobody for a long while. And nobody left in a hurry."

script:
CatchReleaseCMD carryHarpoon
AddTextSmall "Acquired harpoon head, unregistered" highlight
text:
It comes out of the plating clean, which your ops chief says twice and does not explain either time. Forty tonnes of barbed alloy, and it lifts like it wants to go.

Your comms officer finds a maintenance mark on the shaft: a fisheries concern, still filing paperwork, which is not a category that has meant anything for two hundred years.

Your comms officer catches it on the way past - a personal-issue beacon, on a loop, running down. It has been transmitting for years.

Underneath it, dug into the regolith, is a smuggler's cache that somebody stopped coming back for, and a man who has been living inside it. He is upright, which is generous of him. Your medical officer takes one look at the empties and declines to estimate how long that will last.
options:
catchrelease_ratingAsk:Ask how he got here
catchrelease_ratingOffer:Offer him passage off the rock
catchrelease_ratingLeave:Leave

text:
"Put off," he says, like it is a place. "Put off. I looked in the tank. That is all. They land the thing and they cover it and you do not look, and I looked."

He does not say what was in it. He starts to, twice.

"The Fisherman." He says it the way you would say the name of a place you are not going back to. "Go and look at it yourself, if you are the looking sort. Everybody is, the first time."

"They keep boats where people are - out past the last colony, where nothing is in the way." He watches your comms officer write the bearing down and does not offer to repeat it.

He looks at your ship for a while and then at the ground. "No," he says. "Thank you. No."

He does not explain that either, and it is somehow the most informative thing he has said.

notes: Walking up to a trawler goes straight into the conversation, which is what OpenComms is for - it sets the flag the encounter reads at the end of its own init and takes the OPEN_COMM branch instead of building the fleet screen. Without this row the boat gets the ordinary engage/disengage/leave screen with an unlabelled comm link at the bottom of it, and everything the boat is for sits behind a line that reads like every hauler in the sector.

text: The trawler's comm crackles. "Evening. Lights are good tonight. Buying, selling, or just drifting?"

The trawler's comm crackles. "Evening. Lights are holding, near enough. Buying, selling, or just drifting?"

The comm image sits a half-second behind them, the way a bad relay does - except there is no relay out here.

The trawler's comm crackles, twice, out of order. "Evening. Lights are good tonight - were good tonight. Buying, selling, or just drifting?"

Their voice arrives a moment before the channel opens, and the lights behind them sweep out of time with the ones outside the window.

The trawler's comm opens on a face already mid-sentence. "- good tonight, lights are good tonight, lights are - evening. Buying, or selling, or just drifting?"

The picture will not hold. There is somebody on the other end of it and they are answering, and the crew behind them are the crew from a boat that is not this one. Somebody aboard says they have met them before. Somebody else says they have never seen them.

The hail is answered before your comms officer has finished sending it.

"New code on my board, this far out, with the lights on." Whoever is aboard sounds like they have been awake a long time. "Nobody gets past the picket by accident, $playerName. Ask."
notes: First contact. The four drift greetings assume you already know what a fishing boat is doing out here - somebody who found one on their own does not, and until this row existed they were handed the ordinary greeting and left to guess. Scored above the greetings and below the interception, so a boat that came to them still says its own line. The script is the same point the bar rating and the castaway call: hailing a boat is being told where one is.

text:
The boat is not where it was ten minutes ago and nobody aboard mentions it.

"You were about to put a hand in that. You are not equipped for it, and I would rather not fish you out afterwards."
"Shelf is bare. What I had, you bought, and I do not chart new waters mid-trip. The surveyors will catch up."
"Market rate, no haggling. The market cannot hear you out here."
options:
0:catchrelease_fisherSellPick:Open the fish buyer - pick what sells
10:catchrelease_fisherSellCommon:Sell all unmarked commons
20:catchrelease_fisherSellUncommon:Sell all unmarked up to uncommon
100:catchrelease_fisherBack:Continue

text: They lean in. Whatever they have heard, an intel note now carries it.
"Nothing on the wind this month. Ask again when the season turns."

"There is a reading I want and cannot go and take. One $catchreleaseWorkFish, out of $catchreleaseWorkWhere. Whatever you land there will be barely holding - that is the point of it, not the animal."

"$catchreleaseWorkPay, and I will carry one more chart from then on. That part does not go away."
An intel note marks the system.
The $catchreleaseWorkFish goes on the table without being asked for.
It is held up to the light for a long moment and then put away without comment.
"Still want the $catchreleaseWorkFish out of $catchreleaseWorkWhere. It is in there. It will keep being in there."

notes: The rating has a boat behind them, which is the whole reason they are worth talking to and the whole reason they are not in a Church or Path port.

text:
"You are heading out past the picket, are you not." They look at your crew rather than at you, and seem to find whatever they were looking for. "Everyone who does has that look about them."

They turn the glass around without drinking from it. "I crewed a boat that went further. Two seasons of it. It is the water that gets you and not the catch - nothing out there sits still long enough to look at twice, and your eyes go on trying anyway."

"They keep one in every system anybody lives in, out past the last colony where nothing is in the way. Hail it. And do not ask what is in the tank."

script: AddBarEvent catchrelease_crabBar "Ask the man with the crate how the crab business is" "A man with a great many pockets is working the room with a crate of live crabs, and is plainly losing money on every one of them."

text:
"Terrible," he says, without being asked twice. "Crablobab. That is me, and that is the crabs as well, it saves time." One of the crate's occupants has got a claw through the mesh and is working on the rest of itself.

He looks you over - the coat, the boots, whatever it is you have been doing to your hands - and decides something. "You do not want crabs."

text: He takes it well. "Nobody wants crabs," he says, to the room, and goes back to trying to sell them to it.
$otherFleetFactionArticleCap opens with a question about the harpoon, and does not appear to be waiting for an answer to it.
There is a hole in their hull the shape of your fishing gear, and $otherFleetFactionArticle would like you to know that it has been noted.
$otherFleetFactionArticleCap has your transponder code, the puncture, and a great deal to say about the relationship between the two.
Whatever $otherFleetFactionArticle expected to be shot at with today, it was not a rope.
They wait. Somewhere behind them a winch is running, and has been running the whole time.

options: 0:catchrelease_ask_howLong:"How long have you been out here?"

text:
"A while." A pause that goes on slightly too long to be a pause. "The boats are newer than the work. That is usually the way of it."

You do not get a number, and it does not occur to you until later that you did not get a number.

options: 10:catchrelease_ask_baha:"They call you Baha, in the registry."

text:
Nothing moves in the face for a moment.

"He signed for the first boat. The paperwork has never caught up and I have never asked it to."

The winch stops. It starts again.

options: 20:catchrelease_ask_why0ut:"Why do your boats never go in past the last colony?"

text: "Nothing to catch in there. The fabric is thick where people are - all that living presses it down flat." A shrug. "And they do not like the lamps. Nobody ever says why."

options: 30:catchrelease_ask_looking:"What happens to somebody who looks at the catch?"

text:
"They look at it."

That appears to be the whole answer. Then, after a while:

"It is not the looking. It is that the thing looks back, and it does not know how to stop, and it does not know that you are not water."

"Habits, mostly. Something on the other side did a thing so many times that the shape of the doing survived the doer." A hand turns over. "Then it drifts in here, and here has rules about having a body, so it grows one."

"That is why they come apart when the water is bad. Nothing is holding the shape but the habit."

"It is not worse. It is thinner. You can see further through it and there is more on the other side to see."

"People say worse because of what it does to them, which is a different subject and not one the water is interested in."

The answer takes long enough that you assume the channel has dropped.

"Not the way you mean."

The lights outside the window sweep past, and for the length of that sweep the crew behind them are standing in a different order.

options: 70:catchrelease_ask_largest:"What is the largest thing you have landed?"

text: "Nothing I brought aboard." They say it as though answering a different question. "You do not land the big ones. You get a reading off them and you cut the line, and if you are quick about it they do not follow the line back."

"$catchreleaseTarget. There is a rupture open in $catchreleaseTargetWhere and it is sitting in it."

"It will keep sitting in it. They do not wander, the ones I ask for - they are already where they were going."

"$catchreleaseTarget. Open water, $catchreleaseTargetWhere. Nothing will show it to you but the lamps, and it will not be pleased about the lamps."

"Take your time. It is not going anywhere it has not already been."

You put the head on the table before anybody has said anything. It is not asked where it came from, and your ops chief notices that and says nothing about it either.

It is turned over once. "They intruded on what they should not have intruded upon."

Nothing further is offered. The silence afterwards is not the kind you fill.
options:
catchrelease_intro_listen:"What is out here?"
catchrelease_intro_brief:"Skip the speech. What is it you need?"

text: "You have questions," they say, before your comms officer has finished the hail. "Everybody who gets this far has the same three, $playerName, so I will save you two of them."
options:
catchrelease_intro_listen:"What is out here?"
catchrelease_intro_brief:"Skip the speech. What is it you need?"

text:
"The fabric is thin in places, and has been since the gates went. Where it is thinnest, things come through it - alive, mostly, and they do not hold together well on this side."

"We call them fish. It is not accurate. It stuck."

"The second question is whether it is safe, and it is not. The third one you will not think to ask until considerably later."
They do not appear to mind being cut off, which is its own kind of answer.

A crate comes up onto the deck before the sentence is finished, and your ops chief signs for it without being asked to. One rod, secondhand, working.

"Near a rupture it opens the thing. Over an open one it puts drones down. It reads the situation, so you do not have to."

"Bring me $catchreleaseTarget out of $catchreleaseTargetWhere. There is a rupture there with your name on it."

CatchReleaseCMD tokens
Highlight "$catchreleaseTarget" "$catchreleaseTargetWhere"
text:
It is weighed, turned over, and set down. "Good. Now the part nobody explains."

"The drones are the same rod you already have. Over open water they hunt; under lamps they search. One tool, three moods, and it picks the mood itself."

"And the fish are not fish. They are patterns the ghosts assume when something on this side is looking at them. That is why they come apart when you land them, and why the water they came out of matters a great deal more than they do."

"Which is the lesson. $catchreleaseTarget, out of $catchreleaseTargetWhere. The water there is thinner. See what that does to it."
"Call them whatever holds still in your head." They are already looking past you at the window. "They do not answer to either of us, and they have never once answered to me."

CatchReleaseCMD giveDeepGear
CatchReleaseCMD tokens
Highlight "$catchreleaseTarget" "$catchreleaseTargetWhere"
text:
They hold it up to the light for a while and do not say what they are looking for. Your science officer, watching over your shoulder, quietly stops taking notes.

"Thinner water, worse coherence, same animal. You have seen it now."

A second crate comes up. Lamps, a harpoon, and a ledger.

"The lamps burn a window through where there is no rupture to use. The line takes whatever the window shows you. Everything in the ledger is bought with the catch - there is no other currency out here, whatever they told you inside the picket."

"Bring me $catchreleaseTarget out of $catchreleaseTargetWhere. Through a lamp, on a line. A thing out of a pond will not answer the question I am asking."

script:
CatchReleaseCMD takeTarget
CatchReleaseCMD giveCharts
CatchReleaseCMD tokens
Highlight "$catchreleaseTarget" "$catchreleaseTargetWhere"
text:
It goes into a case rather than onto the table, and the case is closed before your science officer can get a reading off it.

"That is the whole trade. Everything after this is doing it better."

"Survey data is where a thing lives - the water, the star, the age of the place. Read a chart and you know where to point yourself, instead of sweeping until you are out of fuel and patience. Two of them, on the house."

"Bring me both. And use the planner on your map before you go. There are two of them now, and doing that by eye is how people end up in the abyss."

script:
CatchReleaseCMD takeTarget
CatchReleaseCMD finishIntro
CatchReleaseCMD tokens
AddTextSmall "Survey counter opened" highlight
text:
Both of them are looked at properly, which has not happened before.

"Then you can read the water. The counter is open to you, $playerName - charts for charts, and I will carry what I can."

Four more go across the table unasked: two common, one uncommon, and one they do not name.

"Still out there, then." They do not sound surprised, or impatient, or much of anything.

"$catchreleaseTarget. $catchreleaseTargetWhere. It is in there, and it will keep being in there."

"Take your time. The water is not going anywhere and neither, apparently, are you."

"$catchreleaseTarget. $catchreleaseTargetWhere."

"Both of them, I did say." A pause. "Your navigator will thank you for using the planner."

"$catchreleaseTarget. $catchreleaseTargetWhere."

"Not yet."

"$catchreleaseTarget. $catchreleaseTargetWhere. It is in there."
options:
catchrelease_intro_fourJumps:"I left you four jumps back."
catchrelease_fisherBack:Continue

text:
"You left a boat four jumps back," they say, and go back to the window.

Your comms officer checks the transponder twice, then stops checking it.
"Still at it. Good. The charts are what I sell and the water is what I know - between the two that is most of a map."

text:

"Then you will not want the speech."

notes: A patrol that has seen the lamps lit somewhere they are not allowed, arriving. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger, which puts the fleet's own memory in the local scope. Marked as had here rather than at each ending, as the cargo scan does: the patrol is still pursuing while the dialog is open, so a conversation that only counted once it was finished would reopen the instant the player closed it. The command runs after the hail so the standing it costs is printed under that line rather than over it.

text:
"Cut the lamps. Now, and then we'll talk."

$PersonRank $personName is not looking at you. $HeOrShe is looking at something off to one side, and whatever it is saying does not appear to be good news.

"Whatever those are, they are reading on our instruments as a hull breach the size of a landing bay, and they are doing it within sight of $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere. Consider that the warning."

"Hegemony Navy. Cut the lamps."

$PersonRank $personName reads from a screen with the flat delivery of somebody who has read it before. "Operation of an unregistered field device within sight of a registered population centre. That is $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere, and there are people on it."

$HeOrShe looks up. "Kill the power and we file it as a first instance. That is the whole of what I am authorised to offer."

"Cut the lights, please."

The voice is pleasant and does not slow down for any of it. "You are operating an unlicensed aperture device inside a corporate exclusion zone. Tri-Tachyon holds four patents adjacent to whatever that is, none of which you have, and the liability position over $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere is - I am told - unattractive."

$PersonRank $personName waits. "Switch it off and this stays a note in a file nobody reads."

"In the name of Ludd, put that out."

There is no preamble and no rank offered. $PersonRank $personName's voice is steady in the way of somebody holding it steady.

"We have seen what that light does. It is a wound, and you are carrying it through creation as though it were a lantern. Put it out and we will not ask what you were looking for."

"Turn it off."

$PersonRank $personName does not appear to have blinked since the link opened. "That's a hole. You've cut a hole in the world and you're dragging it around behind you like it's luggage."

"Off. Now. Or we come and put it out for you, and we're not gentle about doors."

"Kill the lights."

$PersonRank $personName does not sound official about it, which is somehow worse. "Whatever that is, it has every sensor in this system screaming, and some of the ones screaming are ours. There's people under $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere who pay us for that not to happen."

"Off. I'd rather not explain to them why it kept happening."

"Cut it. Cut it now."

$PersonRank $personName says that before saying anything else, and only then remembers the rest of it. "This is a Diktat patrol. You are operating an unauthorised device over $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere. There is no permit for that device because there is no such device."

$HeOrShe lets that stand. "Switch it off and I will not have to decide what to write."

"League patrol. Please cut power to whatever that is."

$PersonRank $personName is polite about it and clearly reading from a card. "We are obliged to inform you that unlicensed operation of a fabric-active device within the approaches to $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere is prohibited under convention, and that a first instance carries a warning."

$HeOrShe puts the card down. "That was the first instance. Please put it out."

"Hey. Turn that off."

$PersonRank $personName is not reading from anything and does not appear to be enjoying this. "I don't know what that is and I don't want to. What I know is my instruments went white and there's a station full of people at $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere who felt it."

"Nobody's written anything down yet. Put it out."

"Lamps off. Somebody has already had to tell you that once."

$PersonRank $personName has the previous stop up on a screen and does not bother pretending otherwise. "There is a schedule for the second one. $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits, paid here, and the lamps go dark before you leave the link."

"Or we do it the way the schedule says to do it when nobody pays."

"Hegemony Navy. You have been warned about this once already."

$PersonRank $personName does not read off the screen this time. "Second instance of the same offence, which takes it off my discretion and onto a schedule. $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay it, kill the lamps, and it stays an administrative matter. Decline, and it becomes a matter for the ships behind me, which I am also authorised to offer."

"Again."

The pleasantness has been switched off somewhere between stops. "Second incident. Policy at this point is a settlement rather than a note, and the settlement is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName lets a moment go by. "The alternative is a write-off, and I should say plainly that the asset being written off in that scenario is you."

"You were asked once."

$PersonRank $personName sounds less angry than tired. "The Church does not fine people for sin. It fines them for damage. There is damage, and it comes to $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay it, put the light out, and go. We would all prefer that."

"You didn't listen."

$PersonRank $personName is smiling, which the link renders badly and which does not help. "So here's how it goes now. $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits, and the lamps go dark, and that buys you off this once."

"Say no and we take the rig apart with you still bolted to it."

"Twice."

$PersonRank $personName sounds genuinely put out. "I let it go the first time because I couldn't be bothered. Now there's paperwork, and paperwork out here means somebody wants paying."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits and the lights go out. Or we take it out of the hull."

"You were told."

$PersonRank $personName says it as a charge rather than a complaint. "Second operation of the same device in Diktat space. The penalty for a second is fixed, and it is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"There is no third schedule. There is only a third response."

"League patrol. We have you on record from the last time."

$PersonRank $personName has put the card away. "A second instance is a fine rather than a warning - $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits - and the device goes cold before you break the link."

"I would take that. The convention is much shorter about what follows it."

"You again."

$PersonRank $personName rubs $hisOrHer eyes. "Look. I am not paid enough to have a position on what that thing is. But somebody at $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere filed something after the last time, and now I have a number to collect."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits, lights out, everybody goes home."

"Cut the lamps and stand by to be boarded."

$PersonRank $personName is past explaining. "Twice was a fine. Three times is an inspection, and I am told to be specific about what we are inspecting for."

"Whatever you have been pulling out through those holes. All of it."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to and prepare to be boarded."

$PersonRank $personName reads the authority out in full, which takes some time, and then stops reading. "Third instance. At a third the schedule stops fining and starts confiscating, and what it confiscates is the reason you keep doing it."

"Every specimen in that hold. Cut your lamps and open your bays."

"Please hold station for boarding."

"Three incidents is where the policy changes character," $PersonRank $personName says. "We are no longer settling. We are recovering. Anything recovered from an unlicensed aperture is - and I am quoting - a corporate asset improperly held."

$HeOrShe sounds, for the first time, interested. "Research would very much like to see what you have."

"Stand down and open your holds."

$PersonRank $personName does not raise $hisOrHer voice for it. "Three times now. We have stopped believing you will put it out because we asked."

"Whatever you have taken from behind that light does not belong on a ship with people aboard it. We will be removing it."

"Cut it and open up."

$PersonRank $personName has given up the pretence that there is a procedure here. "Third time. Third time we take the catch, because that's the part you actually care about, and it's the part that shouldn't exist."

"Every last one of them. Off the ship."

"Lamps off. We're coming aboard."

$PersonRank $personName has stopped being annoyed and started being interested, which is a change for the worse. "Third time is where we stop asking about money and start asking what's in the hold."

"Word is you've been pulling things out of that light. We'd like to see them."

"Cut power and prepare for inspection."

$PersonRank $personName offers no reason and does not appear to think one is owed. "Third contravention. The third response is seizure of materials."

"Open the hold. Do not make me specify which hold."

"League patrol. Prepare to be boarded."

$PersonRank $personName has stopped apologising for the convention. "A third instance provides for seizure of anything obtained by means of the prohibited device. That is the whole of the catch, and it is not a discretionary provision."

"Cut the lamps and open the hold."

"Off. Now. And open the hold."

$PersonRank $personName sounds like somebody working from instructions $heOrShe did not write. "Third time, and this time they gave me orders instead of a number. They want whatever is in there."

"I'm sorry. I've read what those lights do."

text: Your lamps go dark. A shuttle crosses, and for the better part of an hour there are strangers in the hold with lists.
notes: Two beats rather than one, which is the rhythm vanilla's own inspection uses: the narration here, then the losses, then the closing line. Splitting them is not cosmetic - a row's text is added after its script has run, so seizing in this row would print the losses above the paragraph describing the boarding.
No text of its own: the command prints the losses, and the fired rows say what was said over them.

text:
Nobody aboard the patrol looks at the crates for longer than they have to, and nobody signs anything in front of you.

"That will be all," $PersonRank $personName says, and the link closes.

They find tanks, and racks, and a great deal of ice, and nothing in any of it.

"Nothing aboard," somebody reports, and $PersonRank $personName takes rather longer than necessary to accept that. The link closes.

Weapons come up across the formation.
notes: Refusing is not an exit at any rung - the lamps are still lit and still visible, which is the whole of what they came about.

text: A man with a fisher's tan and no boat to show for it has been nursing the same drink since before you came in, and keeps checking a slate that is not telling him anything new.
A licensed fisher sits with her registration papers squared on the table in front of her, which is what people do when the licence is the only part of the operation still working.
A woman with a fisher's hands is going through a ledger backwards, which is how you read one when you are looking for the last month that made money.

options: catchrelease_campPirate_ask:Ask him what the slate is telling him.

text: A fisher is explaining something to a bored-looking clerk, quietly and for what is clearly not the first time, and the clerk is not writing any of it down.
A fisher in a patched flight jacket has a Navy grievance form in front of her and has filled in perhaps a third of it. The third she has filled in has been crossed out twice.
A man who has plainly not been paid this month is buying a round anyway, which is either optimism or the last of it.

options: catchrelease_campMerc_ask:Ask what the clerk is not writing down.

text: A fisher is sitting well away from the door with her back to the wall, and has chosen the seat rather than fallen into it.
A fisher with a licence pinned to his jacket is sitting very still, and every time the door opens he looks at it and then makes himself stop looking at it.
A man with a fisher's squint is drinking steadily and telling nobody in particular that he is not going back out there.

options: catchrelease_campPath_ask:Ask why she picked that seat.

text:
"Same rupture for nine years," he says. "You learn one piece of water properly and it keeps you. Then somebody who has never fished anything in their life parks on it because it is a nice quiet spot to park."

"$catchreleaseCampManyCap. In $catchreleaseCampWhere. Flying dark and not going anywhere."

He turns the slate around. It is a fuel invoice, and the number on it is not one he can pay twice. "I do not care how. Kill them, buy them off, tell them a story - I have stopped having a preference. Just bring me $catchreleaseAsk out of that water afterwards, so I know it was that water."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap, and it is most of what I have left."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to clear the spot.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Find other water."

text:
The clerk leaves without looking back. The fisher does not watch.

"They are not pirates," she says. "That is the whole problem. Pirates you can report. These ones have a contract, and a contract means somebody who is not out there gets to decide what happens to my water, and nobody will tell me who."

"$catchreleaseCampManyCap, sitting on a rupture in $catchreleaseCampWhere, perfectly polite about it. They told me to come back in a year."

She looks at you properly for the first time. "I do not need them arrested. I need them gone, and I am not going to ask how. Bring me $catchreleaseAsk out of it when it is done - that is how I will know. $catchreleaseRewardCap."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to move them off.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Somebody is paying them. Somebody will pay the next lot too."

text:
"Because I want to see the door," she says. "You asked."

She does not lower her voice, which somehow makes it worse. "There is a cell sitting on my rupture in $catchreleaseCampWhere. $catchreleaseCampManyCap. They are not robbing anybody. They are there because they have decided the water is an offence, and that anything that comes out of it is an offence, and that people who go in after it are the same."

"They let me leave. They were very clear that it was a decision they made."

"I want my water back. However that happens. And I want $catchreleaseAsk out of it in my hands afterwards, because I would like to hold the thing they said should not exist. $catchreleaseRewardCap."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to go and see them.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Not against the Path."

text: "Nine years," he says again, to himself, and goes back to the invoice.
He turns the slate back around without any particular bitterness. It is not the first no.
"Still sitting there?" He does not sound surprised. "They would be. It is a nice quiet spot to park."
notes: Two reminders rather than one, because there are two things outstanding and being told about the wrong one is worse than not being told.

text: "Water is clear, then." He almost smiles. "Bring me $catchreleaseAsk out of it and I will believe it properly."

He takes the crate with both hands, opens it on the table in front of everybody, and looks at what is inside for long enough that the noise around the table stops.

"That is my water," he says, and pays you $catchreleaseReward without counting it.
"They will be polite to you as well," she says. "Do not let that do anything to you."
"No," she agrees. "Probably not." She goes back to the form.
"They are still there," she says. It is not a question and she does not wait for an answer.
notes: Two reminders rather than one, because there are two things outstanding and being told about the wrong one is worse than not being told.

text: "Gone." She sits with that for a second. "Then bring me $catchreleaseAsk out of it, and I will go back out."

She does not open the crate in the bar. She signs for it, pays you $catchreleaseReward, and carries it out herself, and through the window you can see her stop halfway across the dock and open it there instead.
"Do not talk to them about it," she says. "Whatever you decide to do. Do not get into it with them about the water."
She nods, as though you have confirmed something. "No. Nobody is."
"They are still on it," she says, and looks at the door.
notes: Two reminders rather than one, because there are two things outstanding and being told about the wrong one is worse than not being told.

text: "Off my water." She says it once, flatly, testing it. "Then bring me $catchreleaseAsk out of it. I would like to see one."

She opens the crate herself, in the middle of the bar, with the door in plain sight and no apparent interest in it any more.

She looks at the specimen for a long time. Then she closes the lid, pays you $catchreleaseReward, and says: "It is just a fish."

notes: Vanilla's own shape for a fleet camping something the player wants - the gate-sitting pirates in the Galatia arc open exactly like this. HailPlayer rather than OpenComms because the hail is what opens the link regardless of the relationship, which is the only reason a conversation with a hostile pirate pack is possible at all. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger, which puts the fleet's own memory in the local scope.

text:
Whoever answers does not introduce themselves.

"You are the second fleet out here this month and the first one did not stay either. This is ours now. It was not, and then nobody came, and now it is."

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits and we will find somewhere else to not be bothered."

"Well, look at this." The man on the screen has his boots up on something that was not designed for boots. "Somebody has actually come out. We had a bet."

"Here is where we are. There is a hole in space out here that nobody owns, nobody patrols, and nobody comes looking in. Do you know what that is worth? Because it is not worth what is in the water. It is worth being somewhere nobody looks."

$HeOrShe takes the boots down. "$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits buys us a different nowhere. That is the whole offer, and I would take it, because the other thing we are good at is this."

"Contracted denial of the site. You are welcome to the file number, I am not permitted to give you the client."

$PersonRank $personName is unhurried and entirely professional about it, which is the worst part. "Nobody is being robbed. Nobody is being shot at. We are here, and while we are here nobody fishes it, and that is the whole of the service."

"There is a figure at which the contract stops being worth more than the alternative, and it is $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits. I am telling you that because it is not a secret and because I would rather be paid than shot at. Either is survivable."

The woman on the screen is not armed and is standing in front of somebody who is.

"You have come for the water," she says. "Everyone does. It opens up out of nothing, and there are things living in it that were never born, and every single one of you decides the correct response is a net."

"We are not stopping you fishing. We are stopping this. This hole, this water, these things. Somebody has to sit in front of it."

She says the next part like a formality, and like she already knows the answer. "You will offer us money. People do. $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits, or whatever the figure is. Offer it if you like."

notes: Greyed out with a reason rather than hidden, the way vanilla handles a bribe the player cannot cover.

notes: The third way through, for a fleet that can neither win the fight nor cover the bribe. Same bonus XP key the enforcement stops use - it is the same kind of thing being talked out of.

Vanilla's own option and vanilla's own handler. Leaving is a real answer here: nothing about the job says the camp has to be dealt with today, and the fourth way through is coming back later with a bigger fleet.

"Pleasure." The formation is already coming about.

text:
You do not argue about the water. You talk about the rupture instead - what it is, how long the ones like it stay open, and what has been recorded coming out of the ones that stayed open longest.

None of it is a threat and all of it is true, which is what makes it work. Somewhere in the middle the person on the screen stops interrupting, and by the end they are looking past you at the water rather than at you.

"We were going to move on anyway," they say, to nobody, and the formation begins to come about.
